sources.title: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall 1999, 596 pp.; full scanned text)
sources.locator: Section 3.4 (printed pp. 146-152) for the multipole expansion and Section 4.1.3 (printed pp. 163-165) for the external torque and force on a dipole. Read in the stamped scanned full text, OCR cross-checked.

contents.name: Example 3.10: the exact potential of two opposite charges and its far-field dipole approximation (printed pp. 146-147, Eqs. (3.89)-(3.90))
contents.support: The exact two-charge potential, its far-field expansion and the identification of the leading dipole term are the worked example of the B companion.

contents.name: Eqs. (3.91)-(3.96): the systematic multipole expansion of the potential in powers of 1/r with Legendre polynomials P_n(cos theta') (printed pp. 147-149)
contents.support: The exterior all-order spherical expansion with its convergent tail bound is the theorem; the Legendre kernel and addition-theorem machinery come from the earlier mathematics suppliers.

contents.name: Eq. (3.97) monopole term and Eq. (3.98) dipole moment p = integral r' rho d tau'; Eq. (3.100) p = sum q_i r_i' for point charges (printed pp. 149-150)
contents.support: The total charge, the dipole moment of a distribution and of a finite point-charge system are clauses (a) and (c) of the definition.

contents.name: Eq. (3.99) dipole contribution to the potential and the comparison with the physical dipole; the remark that higher multipoles are present at finite separation (printed p. 150)
contents.support: The monopole-dipole truncation with an explicit remainder, and the reason the expansion is only approximate for a finite dipole, are the content of the dipole expansion theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.4.3: origin of coordinates in multipole expansions; the shift p -> p - Q a and the origin independence of p when Q = 0 (printed pp. 151-152)
contents.support: The dipole transformation under an origin shift and the exact condition for its invariance are clauses (b) of the origin-shift theorem.

contents.name: Fig. 3.27: monopole, dipole, quadrupole and octopole hierarchy (printed p. 147)
contents.support: The hierarchy is absorbed into the theorem as the uniform decay of the exterior series, made quantitative by the geometric tail bound.

contents.name: Section 4.1.3: torque N = p x E (4.4) and force F = (p . nabla) E (4.5) on a dipole in a field, and the reference-point shift N = (p x E) + (r x F) (printed pp. 163-165)
contents.support: The external-field torque and force on a small dipole, computed here for a prescribed compact distribution with a Lipschitz external field and an explicit remainder, are the content of the torque theorem.

contents.name: Problems 3.26-3.29 (approximate potentials of particular configurations; quadrupole and octopole terms for the physical dipole) and Problems 4.5-4.7 (torque and energy exercises for ideal dipoles) (printed pp. 149-151, 165)
contents.reason: Exercise statements for particular configurations; the general expansion theorems and the two worked examples of this pair cover the general content, and no exercise solution is part of the promised claims.

sources.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 printing, 236 pp.)
sources.locator: Sections 2.2.2 and 2.2.3 (printed pp. 18-22) for the physical dipole and the multipole expansion, and Section 2.3.2 (printed pp. 28-29) for the force between two dipoles. Read in the stamped full text.

contents.name: Section 2.2.2 The Dipole: exact two-charge potential and its far-field expansion (printed pp. 18-19)
contents.support: The exact potential of two opposite charges and its far-field behaviour are the worked two-charge dipole example.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3: the Taylor expansion (2.22) of 1/|r - r'| and the far-field series phi = (1/4 pi epsilon_0)(Q/r + p . r-hat / r^2 + ...) (printed pp. 20-22)
contents.support: The monopole-dipole truncation of the far-field potential is the dipole expansion theorem.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3: the dipole moment p = integral r' rho and the discussion of the neutral case Q = 0 (printed p. 21-22)
contents.support: The dipole moment as a source moment of the density is clause (a) of the definition.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3: the symmetric traceless quadrupole Q_ij = integral rho (3 r'_i r'_j - delta_ij r'^2) (printed p. 22)
contents.support: The traceless quadrupole is clause (a) of the definition.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3: the quadrupole potential term Delta phi = r_i r_j Q_ij / (2 . 4 pi epsilon_0 r^5) and the remark that the systematic multipole expansion uses spherical harmonics (printed p. 22)
contents.support: The degree-two term of the exterior spherical series is identified with the traceless quadrupole in clause (b) of the general multipoles theorem.

contents.name: Section 2.2.4 Field Lines (printed p. 23)
contents.reason: Qualitative field-line and equipotential pictures; the pair proves no field-line regularity statement and uses no pictorial material.

contents.name: Section 2.3.2 The Force Between Electric Dipoles: interaction energy and F = -grad U for two separated dipoles (printed pp. 28-29)
contents.reason: Two-dipole interaction through a mechanical potential differential; the pair's torque theorem concerns one prescribed distribution in an external field, and no mutual-interaction or dynamics claim is promised.

sources.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, 3rd revised English edition (Pergamon 1971, 387 pp.; full text)
sources.locator: Sections 40 and 41 (printed pp. 95-100) for the dipole and quadrupole moments, the dipole field and the general spherical-harmonic multipole expansion; Gaussian units re-expressed in SI. Read in the stamped full text.

contents.name: Section 40: the dipole moment d = sum e_a r_a (40.3) (printed p. 95)
contents.support: The dipole moment of a charge system is clause (c) (and, for densities, clause (a)) of the definition.

contents.name: Section 40: origin independence of the dipole moment when the total charge vanishes (printed p. 95)
contents.support: The invariance condition is clause (b) of the origin-shift theorem.

contents.name: Section 40: the potential phi = d . R / R^3 (40.7) and the dipole field (40.8)-(40.11) of a neutral system at large distances (printed pp. 95-97)
contents.support: The dipole term of the exterior potential and its far-field character are the content of the dipole expansion theorem.

contents.name: Section 41: the quadrupole moment D_ab = sum e(3 x_a x_b - r^2 delta_ab) (41.3) and its tracelessness D_aa = 0 (41.4) (printed pp. 97-98)
contents.support: The traceless quadrupole of an absolutely continuous density or a finite point-charge system is clause (a) and (c) of the definition.

contents.name: Section 41: origin independence of the quadrupole moment when the total charge and the dipole moment both vanish (printed p. 99)
contents.support: The invariance statement is clause (d) of the origin-shift theorem.

contents.name: Section 41: the general 2^l-pole moments Q_lm and the spherical-harmonic expansion (41.9)-(41.13) (printed pp. 99-100)
contents.support: The all-order exterior spherical expansion and its coefficients are the general multipoles theorem.

contents.name: Section 41: remarks on irreducible symmetric traceless rank-l tensors with 2l+1 components and on principal axes of D_ab (41.7)-(41.8) (printed pp. 98-99)
contents.reason: Structural remarks on irreducible tensors and principal axes; the pair uses the traceless quadrupole only through its defining integral, its origin transformation and its potential term, so no eigenvalue interpretation is needed.

contents.name: Example 3.10, the physical dipole and Eq. (3.101) p = qd (printed pp. 146-147, 149-150)
contents.support: The exact two-charge potential, the moment p = qd and the remark that the dipole potential is only approximate at finite separation are the two-charge dipole example.

contents.name: Fig. 3.30 with the surrounding discussion: four charges at the corners of a square whose net dipole moment vanishes, a quadrupole configuration (printed pp. 150-151)
contents.support: The explicit four-charge configuration with vanishing dipole moment and nonzero traceless quadrupole is the quadrupole symmetry example.

contents.name: Problems 3.27-3.29 (approximate potentials of particular charge configurations) (printed p. 151)
contents.reason: Exercise statements for particular configurations; the pair's two examples cover the general techniques and no exercise solution is promised.

contents.name: Section 2.2.2: the physical dipole of two opposite charges and its moment p = Qd (printed pp. 18-19)
contents.support: The exact potential and moment of the two-charge dipole are the content of the two-charge dipole example.

contents.support: The two-charge moment p = qd is the content of the two-charge dipole example.

contents.name: Section 41: the quadrupole moment D_ab computed by inserting each charge, and D_aa = 0 (41.3)-(41.4) (printed p. 98)
